newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong home mortgage lending dip in August.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong home mortgage lending dip in August.

text.p: Home mortgage lending in Hong Kong grew by only 0.6 percent in August, down from the monthly average increase of 1.4 percent in the last 12 months, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) said on Wednesday.
Lending by 33 institutions in the survey stood at HK$304.8 billion in August, it said.
"Loan growth eased in August, reflecting the reduced activity in the primary property market in the preceding month," David Carse, deputy chief executive of HKMA, said.
Annualised rate of growth in lending over a three month period ending August fell to 14.3 percent from 17.7 percent in the three-month period to July, the HKMA said in a statement.
The 12-month average of outstanding loans showed an annualised growth rate of 16.2 percent, compared with 16.6 percent in the 12-month period ending in July.
Amount of new loans approved but not yet drawn fell by HK$2.6 billion, or 24.3 percent, to HK$8.1 billion in August.
Lending for purchase of China properties went up by 1.1 percent to HK$5.8 billion in August.
Gross loans in August went up marginally to 346 from 344 but fell in amount to HK$165 million from HK$235 million.
